Frontier AI performance just got commoditized. Again.

Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5 this week. It scores within 0.5% of Fable 5 on Cursor Bench 3.2, achieved a perfect score on IMO 2026, and topped the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. The price: $5 per million input tokens. Exactly half what the leading competitor charges for comparable performance.

But the pricing is not the real story. The real story is what Anthropic optimized for. Opus 5 is built for longer, more reliable agentic work — lower latency, reduced token consumption, and significantly less human supervision required to complete real tasks. This is a deliberate bet that enterprise customers will choose predictable execution over marginal intelligence gains.

The frontier AI market is splitting into two value propositions. One sells peak intelligence at premium pricing. The other sells reliable task completion at scale. Anthropic is planting its flag firmly in the second camp, and for most enterprise use cases, that is the more valuable position.

For CTOs evaluating AI infrastructure spend: the cost per completed task is now the metric that matters. Not the benchmark score. Not the model size. The cost of getting real work done, reliably, with minimal human intervention.

This repricing accelerates the timeline for AI agent deployment across enterprise workflows. The models are no longer the bottleneck. Organizational readiness is.
